title: [source-mongodb] incremental syncs giving errors - Saved offset is not valid
body:
### Connector Name

source-mongodb

### Connector Version

1.4.0

### What step the error happened?

During the sync

### Relevant information

**_Airbyte Version_** - 0.57.2

After few days of successfully syncing the data, the syncs starts failing. There are two types of errors which i am facing for this in two different connections... attaching info for both below individually.
Sync happens every 6 hours. 

**Error 1**: _Failure in source: Saved offset is not valid. Please reset the connection, and then increase oplog retention and/or increase sync frequency to prevent his from happening in the future_

Oplog seems to have enough data to start the sync... oldest log is from 1st Oct. Syncs started failing from 7th Oct. 2024.

Oplog info - 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f4f2d61-b134-4ad8-bf01-fc54dd9bde1c)



**Error 2**: _An exception occurred in the change event producer_
_Caused by: com.mongodb.MongoCommandException: Command failed with error 280 (ChangeStreamFatalError): 'PlanExecutor error during aggregation :: caused by :: cannot resume stream; the resume token was not found'_


Oplog info - 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed64d865-286b-4c42-a4d8-c502cb502eb7)



In what scenario could this happen ? Could this be due to a case where for a long period of time there was no change in a particular collection say for 10 days. On 11th day a change occurred in that collection. By this time the mongo might have removed the older entry from oplog of that particular collection ?
**Any possible solution ?**

### Relevant log output

_No response_

### Contribute

- [ ] Yes, I want to contribute

comments.author: whanata
comments.body:
I have the same issue with sync from `Mongo DB` to `Snowflake`.
`Saved offset is not valid.`.

Airbyte OSS - `1.5.1`
Mongo DB Source - `2.0.1`
Snowflake DB Destination - `3.15.10`

It happens twice already, a week apart on the same time.
This corresponds to the Oplog Window of 7 days I added in my Mongo DB Cluster.

One thing I noticed is that in `Connection state`, the `shared state` had 2 state.
```
"shared_state": {
  "state": {
    "[\"prod\",{\"server_id\":\"prod\"}]": <resume_token>,
    "[<mongo_url>]": <resume_token>
  },
  "schema_enforced": false
},
```

The `[<mongo_url>]` seems to have a resume token that's up to date (based of my syncs every hour).
The `"[\"prod\",{\"server_id\":\"prod\"}]"` resume token is the same and does not update at all.

I checked what the resume token is by just creating my own Mongo Change Stream and see what the first event was for that Resume Token.

The fix I did for the last 2 weeks was update the resume token of `"[\"prod\",{\"server_id\":\"prod\"}]"` with the Mongo URL Resume token on the other state.

I didn't have this issue when my Mongo DB Source was on version `1`, but I seem to have encountered the issue ever since I've upgraded the Mongo DB Source to version `2` which allows multiple different schemas within one Mongo DB Cluster. I don't utilise multiple schemas within a Mongo DB Cluster, so I'm only using it as having only 1 schema.

I was wondering if anyone knew why the Resume Token for `"[\"prod\",{\"server_id\":\"prod\"}]"` does not update in the first place or what is that specific state for? I assume that's the state of what it is in Snowflake, but I'm not entirely sure.

comments.author: whanata
comments.body:
@raphaelsampaio 
https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte/issues/48496#issuecomment-2879259974
I'm trying this solution (I didn't check the logs when I saw this the first time - my bad), I believe I was experience the same error. I've given my Mongo User permission to read local and I have synced it.

This indeed change that warning to actually being able to see Oplog Size as mentioned in the solution above.

It didn't change the resume token I was expecting (it was still using the old Resume Token).
Only the Resume token on the Mongo URL was updated.

```
"shared_state": {
  "state": {
    "[\"prod\",{\"server_id\":\"prod\"}]": <old_stale_resume_token>,
    "[<mongo_url>]": <new_resume_token>
  },
  "schema_enforced": false
},
```

---

I forgotten to clarify that I am also using Secondary Preferred (we didn't want to put load on our Primary during syncs).

---

What I plan to do to check if the change works is wait for a week (we keep oplogs up to a week) and see if it fails again.
I can verify before that if it happens again, the act of just updating the `resume token` so it matches the one used in the `<mongo_url>` will work.
